facts: Attia calls four chronic diseases the Four Horsemen: heart disease, cancer, neurodegenerative disease such as Alzheimer's, and type 2 diabetes with metabolic dysfunction.
He says the odds are overwhelming that most people will die of one of them.
Medicine 2.0 mostly reacts once disease is established; Medicine 3.0 starts earlier and weighs the risk of doing nothing.
Attia treats metabolic health as foundational.
He calls elevated insulin the canary in the coal mine of metabolic disorder.
Insulin resistance is linked to higher risk of cancer, Alzheimer's and cardiovascular death; this is an association.
One summary calls insulin sensitivity the variable connecting all four horsemen.
Medicine 3.0 uses five tactics: exercise, nutrition, sleep, emotional health and exogenous molecules such as drugs, hormones and supplements.
Half of major adverse cardiovascular events in men and a third in women happen before 65.
In a glucose tolerance test, early insulin resistance shows as a sharp insulin rise in the first 30 minutes that stays high for the next hour.

conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Attia says most people will die of one of four chronic diseases: heart disease, cancer, Alzheimer's or type 2 diabetes. He treats metabolic health as foundational and calls raised insulin the canary in the coal mine. Insulin resistance is linked to higher risk of the others, an association, so he argues for checking early signals instead of waiting.
